name: clawd-hq
description: A chief of staff for Claude Code: keep talking while Clawd hands work to specialists from your installed helpers and runs them in the background, with a live pixel-art office panel.

chiefOfStaff.title: Clawd runs the chat
chiefOfStaff.description: On (default): while the office is open, the main chat works as Clawd, the chief of staff. He hands real work to specialists, asks you only what needs you, and reports in plain words. The office is closed by default, so Clawd comes in when you type /office (or when "Open the office at session start" is on); type /office again to close the office and send him away from your next message on, with specialists already at work carrying on and the plan kept. Off: Claude behaves as usual, open office or not, and you keep the panel.

voiceFile.title: Your own voice file
voiceFile.description: The full path of a text file that sets how Clawd sounds, in place of his built-in voice. It changes his tone only, never his rules. Leave empty for the built-in voice. Read when a session starts, up to 8000 characters. When set, it wins over your own copy from the Settings tab, and the tab shows and edits this file instead.

quietChat.title: Quiet chat
quietChat.description: On (default): while Clawd runs the chat, it hides the 'finished' notices of specialists he hired, the messages of teammates he hired by name, and his own no-update lines. He reports once the job is done, and the Settings tab lists what finished. A failure or a request for your permission or approval always shows; a specialist's question goes to Clawd, who asks you. And the full view (ctrl+o) shows everything. Off: the chat shows every row as Claude Code draws it.

youShouldKnow.title: You should know
youShouldKnow.description: On (default): right after Clawd answers you, when a specialist handed work back or Clawd took six or more steps himself, a copy of the main conversation on your session's model looks for the one thing you would regret missing, and may leave one short note on Clawd's card. It reuses the chat Claude Code already cached, so it costs least right after a reply; after a long pause or a /model change it pays for the whole chat again. Learn more, Simpler, Shorter and More detail ask the same way. A separate guard, code only, reads each specialist's own steps for a command that deletes or overwrites for good, the sandbox turned off, or a refused action done another way. Checks are made only while one of the office tabs is open. While it is on and an office tab is open, Claude Code's own "You should know" note above the prompt box stays quiet. Off: no checks are made, and Claude Code's own note works as usual.

leftUndone.title: Left undone check
leftUndone.description: The old model check (your request against Clawd's report) is retired, so this switch does nothing yet. A tracker for forgotten asks is coming and will use it. TODO, skipped-test and not-implemented markers written into code files are read on this machine and are not affected.

autoSetup.title: Automatic setup
autoSetup.description: On (default): the first time the office opens in a project with no saved setup (when you type /office, or at session start if "Open the office at session start" is on), setup runs by itself, with no questions. While the office stays closed nothing runs, and a setup left half done waits too. It looks quietly around the project, picks a starting team, hires it and keeps how you like to work in mind, then leaves one small card on the Office tab saying what was set up. It uses your plan, about $0.15 per project: a read-only Sonnet scout reads the project to pick the team, an Opus call picks it instead only if the scout gives nothing usable, and a Haiku call reads your instruction files for how you like to work. Off: nothing runs by itself, not even a setup left half done, and helpers are not laid off by themselves; type /office-setup to run or finish it when you want.

skillSearch.title: Search the public skill registry when matches are weak
skillSearch.description: On (default): when the installed agents and skills match a job weakly or not at all, Clawd's search for helpers also looks the job up on the public skill registry (skills.sh), with up to three short searches of plain words (the job's keywords, and when they find nothing, words from the job description). The plugin asks Claude Code to fetch the search page, and nothing is downloaded or run. The keywords are sent to skills.sh, more often than when it ran only if nothing matched. If a strong match turns up, he tells you its name, source and install count and asks before he installs anything; nothing is installed without your yes. Off: nothing is searched or sent, and he uses the general-purpose agent with a fuller brief.

openAtStart.title: Open the office at session start
openAtStart.description: On: a new session opens the Office, People, History and Settings panels and asks to bring Office to the front, and Clawd is in from the first message. Off (default): a new session opens no panels, asks for nothing and has no Clawd (Claude behaves as usual), and shows one short tip, "Type /office to open the office and bring in Clawd", until you have opened the office once. Type /office to open the panels and bring in Clawd, and again to close them. A session where you closed the office stays closed when you resume it.
